name: 12-Week Posture & Physique Program
summary: 4 days a week on an upper/lower split, so every muscle is trained twice. Each session takes about 60–75 minutes including the 10-minute warm-up.

schedule.focus: Rest or squash — an easy run or squash is fine
Pull-ups, incline press, extra posture work
Deadlift and hip thrust, plus core

missedDays: If you can only train 3 days in a week, run the four sessions in order and carry on from where you stopped. Don't skip the lower days.

warmup.title: Posture warm-up
warmup.intro: Once before every workout, and on rest days too if you can. It works on rounded shoulders, a stiff upper back, tight hip flexors and a forward head.

items.name: Dead hang
items.notes: From the pull-up bar. Lets your shoulders open up and builds grip.

items.name: Thoracic extension over the bench
items.notes: Upper back on the end of the bench, hands behind your head, lean back slowly.

items.name: Wall slides
items.notes: Keep your back, elbows and wrists against the wall as you slide your arms up.

items.name: Band pull-aparts
items.notes: Light band, shoulder-width grip, straight arms; squeeze your shoulder blades for 1 s. No band: incline-bench Y-raises, 2 × 12 at 2–4 kg.

items.name: Couch stretch
items.notes: For your hip flexors. Squeeze your glute on the stretching side.

items.name: Chin tucks
items.notes: Pull your head straight back to make a double chin.

items.name: Glute bridge
items.notes: Gets your glutes working before lower days.

workoutsIntro: Main lifts use 6–10 reps, finishing every set with only 1–2 reps left in the tank. If your first set lands more than 2 reps above the top of the range, add weight. Rest 2–3 min between main lifts and 60–90 s between accessories.

days.label: Lower A

exercises.name: Goblet box squat, pain-free depth only

days.note: Squat note: the barbell back squat is out for now because it gives you sharp, warm, stinging pain on the right side of your pelvis. Get that checked by a GP or physio before squatting heavy again. Only use the goblet box squat if it's completely pain-free, with the box high enough that the pain doesn't start. If any lower-body exercise brings the pain back, drop it until you've been assessed. Once you're cleared, put the barbell squat back in, starting light.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.prescription: 4 × max reps (stop at 10, then add weight)

supersetNote: Exercises marked 6a/6b and 7a/7b are supersets: do one set of each back to back, then rest. Use the same weight for all sets of a lift.

progression.rule: Once you hit the top of the rep range on every set with good form, increase the weight next session.
items: squat, deadlift, RDL, hip thrust: add 5 kg.
move up to the next weight, then build back up from the bottom of the rep range.
once you can do 4 × 10, hold a dumbbell between your feet and drop back to 4 × 6.
Stuck for 3 sessions on a lift?
take 10% off that lift and build back up.

phases.title: Build
phases.text: Use the starting weights and progress with the rule.

phases.title: Deload
phases.text: Same weights, half the sets. Clean up your technique.

phases.title: Build
phases.text: Keep progressing. Add one extra set of rows and rear-delt flyes each week.

phases.title: Deload and retest
phases.text: Half the sets in the first half of the week. At the end, test 5-rep sets on bench, deadlift and pull-ups.

photos: Take progress photos (front, side and back, same lighting) in week 1 and week 12.
recovery: about 150–190 g a day (1.6–2.0 g per kg at 93 kg), spread over 3–4 meals.
about 300–500 kcal under maintenance, losing about 0.25–0.5 kg a week. If your lifts drop for 2 weeks in a row, eat a little more.
7–9 hours. Your 5 am sessions only work if you're in bed early.
keep squash and 1–2 easy runs a week. No hard runs within 24 hours before a Lower day.
keep logging every set in Strava. Name each session after its day (e.g. "Upper A", "Lower B") so each week is easy to compare with the last.
back, neck or shoulder pain (not normal soreness) → stop that exercise and see a physio. General guidance, not a medical assessment.
